history.rationale: The revised prompt addresses three measured problems: (1) the 43% too-easy rate by adding evidence-based guidance that pure formatting rules (date formats, thousands separators, half-up rounding, etc.) are caught by the agent's self-tests and should not be primary difficulty drivers, while identifying what reliably slips through—strict inequalities, consecutive delimiters, inverted semantics, and semantic interactions; (2) the 21% unfair 0/5 rate by adding a critical warning in GOAL and DESIGN that every test-checked behavior must be stated in the instruction, since unstated format requirements were the dominant cause of unfair failures; and (3) the agent's false-confidence weakness by adding to WHY the measured finding that self-tests share blind spots with the implementation, explaining why traps must be the kind the agent's typical self-tests miss. New trap families 9 (strict inequality) and 10 (inverted semantics) codify the most effective difficulty levers, and family 8 is revised to distinguish hard-to-verify details (which drive difficulty) from easy-to-verify formatting details (which add realism only).

The revision addresses three evidence-based problems. First, **too-hard tasks (0/5)** overwhelmingly come from unstated requirements that tests check anyway—the gate's 20+ added behaviors show this pattern clearly—so I added an explicit completeness checklist and a warning that this is the most common cause of unfair failure. Second, **too-easy tasks (43%)** arise because the agent's ad-hoc verification catches independent rules easily; I restructured the trap families around measured effectiveness, promoting misleading column names, strict inequalities, inverted semantics, and mixed-direction sorts (all 20-65% pass rates) while demoting pure formatting and pure-function traps that the agent unit-tests away. Third, I added the insight that the agent's tests share its blind spots, making **interacting rules** (dedup-before-filter, priority-affects-both-eligibility-and-sort) more effective than independent rules, and capped checklist breadth at 8-11 rules since 12+ caused 0/5 failures.
